pk.context: 150 mg oral, single dose, healthy adults

clues.kinetics: Oral bioavailability is at least 90% regardless of dose. It does not bind plasma proteins, is barely metabolized, and about 90% of a dose is recovered in urine unchanged.
clues.substance: Molecular weight 159.23. A crystalline solid, freely soluble in water, with pKa values of 4.2 and 10.6.
clues.product: Approved under an NDA as capsules from 25 mg to 300 mg in eight strengths, and as a 20 mg/mL oral solution.
clues.safety: No boxed warning. Contraindicated in hypersensitivity to it or its components; angioedema has occurred, and in children increased weight and appetite are among the most common reactions.
clues.indication: Neuropathic pain from diabetic neuropathy or spinal cord injury, postherpetic neuralgia, fibromyalgia, and adjunctive therapy for partial-onset seizures.
clues.mechanism: Binds with high affinity to the alpha 2-delta subunit of voltage-gated calcium channels, but not directly to GABA or benzodiazepine receptors.

tell: A gabapentinoid cleared almost entirely unchanged by the kidneys, so its elimination tracks creatinine clearance.

evidence.pk.tmaxH: peak plasma concentrations occur within 1.5 hours
evidence.pk.halfLifeH: a mean elimination half-life of 6.3 hours in subjects with normal renal function
